html:
A Byzantine official and lifelong friend of Constantine XI, whose short chronicle is an eyewitness record of the last years of Byzantium.

He served the imperial family from his youth, went on missions to the sultan and to Georgia and Trebizond to find Constantine a bride, and was in Constantinople during the siege of 1453. When the city fell he and his family were enslaved. He bought his own freedom, but his son and daughter died in the sultan's household.

He then served Thomas Palaiologos in the Morea until the Ottoman conquest of 1460, and ended his life as a monk on Corfu, where he wrote his memoir. A much longer chronicle under his name was expanded in the 1500s by a later writer, so historians trust the short version more.
sum: A Byzantine official and lifelong friend of Constantine XI, whose short chronicle is an eyewitness record of the last years of Byzantium.
